title: A root in cross-section
caption: From the outside in: the epidermis (some cells make root hairs), the cortex, the endodermis with its Casparian strip, and the vascular cylinder. The xylem forms a star or cross, with the phloem between its arms. The Casparian strip blocks the apoplast pathway, so water must cross the endodermal cell membranes into the symplast.
alt: A circular root section: an outer epidermis with root hairs, a wide cortex of packed cells, a ring of endodermis with dark Casparian strip dots, and a centre where four xylem arms form a cross with four phloem patches between them.
description: Layers from the outside in: epidermis, cortex, endodermis, vascular cylinder.
Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells and increase the surface area for absorption.
The Casparian strip is a waterproof band in the endodermal walls: it forces water into the symplast, so entry to the xylem is controlled.
The xylem forms a star or cross in the centre, with the phloem between its arms.
